subject: Enclave connectivity: CI blockers & Helm network audit
messages:
From: ops@edgecarve.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Enclave CI failures that look networking-related

Hi Laura / Irene,

We started seeing repeated CI failures on our private (VPC) deploy pipeline this morning after a helm release to the enclave chart. Jobs are timing out during pod init (sidecar never pulls config, healthchecks failing).

What we've observed:
- Failures only in the private-enclave pipeline (staging/prod are gated)
- New NetworkPolicy + initContainer changes in the last helm values bump (attached: priv_helm_values.yaml)
- CI logs show kubelet unable to reach metadata endpoint from the init container; several egress connections being dropped. Snippet attached.

Can Redwood review the helm/network policy diffs and CI configuration? This is blocking a release to a pilot customer and we need a short-term mitigation (canary policy rollback or CI allowlist) and a long-term patch.

Attachments: priv_helm_values.yaml, ci-pipeline-log-snippet.txt

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Ops Engineer, EdgeCarve Networks
ops@edgecarve.com

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: ops@edgecarve.com
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Enclave CI failures that look networking-related

Thanks Alex — we're on it.

Quick plan:
1) Irene and Karthik will triage the helm values + network policy diff and identify the minimal change to unblock CI.
2) We'll propose a short-lived CI egress allowlist for the initContainer metadata endpoints so your pipeline can green while we test a proper fix.
3) We want to run the fix in your non-prod staging first and then roll to pilot with rollback hooks.

Can you confirm the CI job id(s) and the IP ranges your CI runners use? If you can grant a short-lived access key for us to pull full CI logs that speeds up root cause. Otherwise we'll work off the snippets.

I've attached the pipeline snippet you sent and opened a Drive folder for working docs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1PrivAudit

Laura Bennett
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@edgecarve.com
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Enclave CI failures that look networking-related

On Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 10:02 AM laura_bennett@redwood.ai wrote:
> Thanks Alex — we're on it.

I've reviewed the attached helm values and the snippets. Initial findings:
- The helm change added a default-deny egress NetworkPolicy that blocks egress from initContainers to the cluster metadata service and the internal config service at 10.10.5.0/24.
- The initContainer uses an HTTPS call to metadata.redwood-local.internal:8443 during bootstrap; blocking outbound to the cluster metadata endpoint causes the container to hang and eventually timeout the pod readiness probe.
- There's also a serviceAccount change that removed hostNetwork:true for the initContainer in the chart, which interacts with the NetworkPolicy semantics.

Short-term mitigation options (in order of safety):
A) Patch the helm values to add an egress rule allowing traffic to metadata.redwood-local.internal:8443 for initContainers and re-run CI.
B) Add a CI runner IP allowlist for those endpoints (less ideal; brittle).
C) Roll back the NetworkPolicy change in the helm release and re-release.

I've attached the helm values excerpt I edited (priv_helm_values.yaml) and a suggested NetworkPolicy delta. If we go with A, we can ship a small helm patch and run a canary via the staging pipeline.

I recommend we do a staged canary + smoke tests. Karthik — you ok owning the canary deploy?

-Irene
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@edgecarve.com
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Enclave CI failures that look networking-related

Laura / Irene / Alex —

I pulled a test cluster and validated Irene's hypothesis. The network-policy change (default-deny egress) plus the SA change is the coupling that causes init containers to lose access to metadata. I generated a minimal policy delta to unblock CI:
- Add egress rule on app init-pods to allow tcp:8443 to 10.10.5.0/24 (metadata)
- Scope the rule to namespace:ci-staging & label:component=init

I've attached a PNG that highlights the diff (network-policy-diff.png) and a helm patch snippet below to apply as a hotfix:
---
# helm patch snippet (kustomize/helmpost)
patch: |
  - op: add
    path: /spec/egress/-
    value:
      - to:
          - ipBlock:
              cidr: 10.10.5.0/24
        ports:
          - protocol: TCP
            port: 8443
---

Plan:
1) Apply patch to staging via a canary pipeline run (I will kick off and watch).
2) Run smoke + functional tests (10–15 mins).
3) If green, apply same patch to the pilot cluster and communicate rollback window (30 mins).

I will own the canary and the rollback play (kubectl patch / helm rollback). Laura — please confirm we have permission to perform the staging patch; Alex, can you schedule a 30-min maintenance window on Fri morning PST?

-Karthik
Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

From: ops@edgecarve.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Enclave CI failures that look networking-related

Thanks all — confirmed: Fri 2026-02-13 maintenance window worked for staging, canary passed. We're good to push to pilot Monday. Two asks before we close this thread:
1) Can Redwood provide a short written mitigation summary for our security/audit team listing the change, justification, and the rollback procedure? We need that as evidence for our compliance pack.
2) After pilot is green, we'll want a follow-up to replace the temporary allowlist with a longer-term fix (either an internal metadata proxy or an explicit managed service account role), plus a short note on why the original helm change caused the regression.

I've attached the CI job id and a final log snippet for your records. Please drop the mitigation summary to our Drive folder and cc security@edgecarve.com.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Alex
Alex Turner
Ops Engineer, EdgeCarve Networks
